# Codebook - online personality survey

Tab-separated, one row per respondent. Item responses are ratings on a five-point scale: 1 = Disagree, 3 = Neutral, 5 = Agree. **0 = missed.**

Items are taken from published self-report personality scales and were presented to respondents in a single block.

| item | text |
|---|---|
| HSNS1 | I can become entirely absorbed in thinking about my personal affairs, my health, my cares or my relations to others. |
| HSNS2 | My feelings are easily hurt by ridicule or the slighting remarks of others. |
| HSNS3 | When I enter a room I often become self conscious and feel that the eyes of others are upon me. |
| HSNS4 | I dislike sharing the credit of an achievement with others. |
| HSNS5 | I feel that I have enough on my hands without worrying about other people's troubles. |
| HSNS6 | I feel that I am temperamentally different from most people. |
| HSNS7 | I often interpret the remarks of others in a personal way. |
| HSNS8 | I easily become wrapped up in my own interests and forget the existence of others. |
| HSNS9 | I dislike being with a group unless I know that I am appreciated by at least one of those present. |
| HSNS10 | I am secretly "put out" or annoyed when other people come to me with their troubles, asking me for my time and sympathy. |
| DDM1 | I tend to manipulate others to get my way. |
| DDM2 | I have used deceit or lied to get my way. |
| DDM3 | I have used flattery to get my way. |
| DDM4 | I tend to exploit others towards my own end. |
| DDP1 | I tend to lack remorse. |
| DDP2 | I tend to not be too concerned with morality or the morality of my actions. |
| DDP3 | I tend to be callous or insensitive. |
| DDP4 | I tend to be cynical. |
| DDN1 | I tend to want others to admire me. |
| DDN2 | I tend to want others to pay attention to me. |
| DDN3 | I tend to seek prestige or status. |
| DDN4 | I tend to expect special favors from others. |

| variable | description |
|---|---|
| `age` | entered as free text |
| `gender` | 1 = Male, 2 = Female, 3 = Other, 0 = missed |
| `accuracy` | self-rated accuracy of own responses, 0-100 |
| `country` | ISO country code |

Rows: 43,710. Countries: US (27,000), GB (6,200), CA (3,800), AU (3,000), DE (830), IN (660), SE (630), PH (560), PL (520), BR (510).

from scipy.stats import norm

def fit_mimic(its,direct=[]):
 dat=X[its+['gender']].copy()
 dat['gender']=(dat.gender==2).astype(float) # female=1
 dat=dat.dropna()
 syn='trait =~ '+' + '.join(its)+'\ntrait ~ gender\n'
 syn+='\n'.join(f'{z} ~ gender' for z in direct)
 m=ModelMeans(syn)

 ins=m.inspect(std_est=True)

  mm,ii,_,_=fit_mimic(its,[z])

<thought>The preliminary MIMIC results identify strong HSNS intercept DIF at HSNS1, HSNS5, HSNS8, and HSNS10, but small residual tests can be significant with this sample size. I’ll now check both uniform and nonuniform DIF using ordinal item models, multiplicity correction, group-specific CFA loadings, and alternative missing-data handling so that the final item list is not driven by one modeling choice.</thought>
<action>PythonREPL</action>
<action_input>{"input_code":"import statsmodels.api as sm
from statsmodels.miscmodels.ordinal_model import OrderedModel
from statsmodels.stats.multitest import multipletests
# ordinal DIF: each item ~ standardized rest score + female + female*rest; complete per item, zero missing
results=[]
for inst,its in [('HSNS',hs),('DD',dd)]:
 for y in its:
  z=X[its+['gender']].copy()
  z['rest']=z[[q for q in its if q!=y]].mean(axis=1,skipna=True)
  z=z[[y,'gender','rest']].dropna()
  z['female']=(z.gender==2).astype(float)
  z['rest']=(z['rest']-z['rest'].mean())/z['rest'].std()
  z['int']=z.female*z['rest']
  try:
   md=OrderedModel(z[y].astype(int),z[['rest','female','int']],distr='logit').fit(method='bfgs',disp=False,maxiter=200)
   results.append([inst,y,md.params['female'],md.pvalues['female'],md.params['int'],md.pvalues['int']])
  except Exception as e: print(y,e)
r=pd.DataFrame(results,columns=['inst','item','uniform_b','uniform_p','interaction_b','interaction_p'])
r['uniform_q']=multipletests(r.uniform_p,method='holm')[1]; r['interaction_q']=multipletests(r.interaction_p,method='holm')[1]
print(r.round(5).to_string(index=False))
# separate CFA fits and standardized loading contrasts
for name,its,fac in specs:
 print('\nLOADINGS',name)
 outs={}
 for g in [1,2]:
  dat=X.loc[X.gender==g,its].dropna()
  syn='\n'.join(f'{f} =~ '+' + '.join(v) for f,v in fac.items())
  mm=Model(syn);mm.fit(dat); jj=mm.inspect(std_est=True)
  outs[g]=jj[(jj.op=='~') & jj.rval.isin(fac.keys())].set_index('lval')['Est. Std']
 print(pd.DataFrame(outs).assign(diff=lambda q:q[2]-q[1]).round(3).to_string())"} </action_input>
